A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a new measure of complexity, based on the loss landscape, which explains the generalization gap of DNNs.
we propose a novel measure to characterize DNNs, and demonstrate its ability to explain the superior performance of some architectures.
module criticality is a promising new complexity measure that explains the generalization performance of DNNs, and that it can be used for architecture search.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the generalization of a network is not only determined by its overall complexity, as measured for example by the number of parameters, but also by the distribution of the criticality of its modules, which is architecture-dependent.
the generalization ability of a network is not a global property, but is instead a local one, which is related to the module-wise criticality of the network.
the generalization of DNNs is related to the shape of the loss landscape, and not to its smoothness, flatness, or curvature.
